## Try It Yourself

::: {.callout-tip}
## How to Practice
1. **Run the diagnostic plots** and check each one
2. **Run the normality test** and interpret the result
3. **Copy to RStudio** for your notebook exercises
:::

### Diagnostic Plots

```{webr-r}
model <- lm(wellbeing ~ stress + sleep_hours + exercise_mins,
            data = wellbeing)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## What to Look For
- **Residuals vs Fitted**: Random scatter — no pattern = linearity OK
- **Normal Q-Q**: Points follow the diagonal line = normality OK
- **Scale-Location**: Horizontal band = homoscedasticity OK
- **Residuals vs Leverage**: No extreme outliers = no influential cases
:::

### Test Normality of Residuals

```{webr-r}
model <- lm(wellbeing ~ stress + sleep_hours + exercise_mins,
            data = wellbeing)
result <- shapiro.test(residuals(model))

cat("Shapiro-Wilk test of residuals:\n")
cat("W =", round(result$statistic, 3), "\n")
cat("p =", round(result$p.value, 3), "\n\n")
cat("Interpretation:", ifelse(result$p.value > 0.05,
    "Residuals do not significantly depart from normality (p > .05).",
    "Residuals may not be normally distributed (p < .05)."))
```

### Generate APA Output

```{webr-r}
model <- lm(wellbeing ~ stress + sleep_hours + exercise_mins,
            data = wellbeing)
s <- summary(model)

f_p <- pf(s$fstatistic[1], s$fstatistic[2], s$fstatistic[3],
          lower.tail = FALSE)
f_text <- if (f_p < 0.001) "p < .001" else paste0("p = ", round(f_p, 3))

cat("=== APA REPORTING VALUES ===\n\n")
cat("Overall model:\n")
cat("  R² = ", round(s$r.squared, 2),
    ", Adjusted R² = ", round(s$adj.r.squared, 2), "\n", sep = "")
cat("  F(", s$fstatistic[2], ", ", s$fstatistic[3], ") = ",
    round(s$fstatistic[1], 2), ", ", f_text, "\n\n", sep = "")

cat("Individual predictors:\n")
for (i in 2:4) {
  name <- c("Stress", "Sleep", "Exercise")[i - 1]
  b  <- round(s$coefficients[i, 1], 2)
  se <- round(s$coefficients[i, 2], 2)
  p  <- s$coefficients[i, 4]
  p_text <- if (p < 0.001) "p < .001" else paste0("p = ", round(p, 3))
  cat("  ", name, ": b = ", b, ", SE = ", se, ", ", p_text, "\n", sep = "")
}
```

## Self-Assessment

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

**1. To produce the four standard diagnostic plots for a model, we use:**

`r mcq(c("diagnostics(model)", answer = "plot(model)", "check(model)", "residuals(model)"))`

**2. In the Normal Q-Q plot, we want the points to:**

`r mcq(c("Form a horizontal line", answer = "Follow the diagonal reference line", "Cluster in the top-right corner", "Be evenly spread above and below zero"))`

**3. The Shapiro-Wilk test assesses the normality of the model's:**

`r mcq(c("Raw scores", "Predicted values", answer = "Residuals", "Coefficients"))`

**4. In APA format, we report R² and the `r fitb("F", width = 3)`-statistic for overall model fit.**

**5. True or False: Perfect normality of residuals is required for regression to be valid.**

`r torf(FALSE)`

:::
